groups.name: NG/OG tube, normal position
groups.rationale: Two spellings of the same class; identical device and position.

groups.name: Bronchial wall thickening
groups.rationale: Peribronchial cuffing is the radiographic name for thickened bronchial walls seen end-on, so the two terms describe the same ring and tram-track appearance.

groups.name: Small pleural effusion / costophrenic blunting
groups.rationale: On a frontal radiograph a small effusion appears as a blunted costophrenic angle, and many reporters write 'blunting' for exactly this appearance.

groups.name: Linear band-like opacity
groups.rationale: Both describe a thin linear or band-like basal opacity; whether it is called plate atelectasis or a parenchymal band or linear scar depends on the reader's habit, not on the image.

considered_not_grouped.reason: Parent and its size or morphology subtypes. Only the small-effusion and blunting pair is merged.
Blunting can also come from pleural thickening or scarring, but it is most often reported for small effusions. Blunting was put with small effusion, not with thickening.

members: Rib splaying / horizontal ribs / widened intercostal spaces
considered_not_grouped.reason: Flattened diaphragms and horizontal ribs are individual signs that together make up hyperinflation. A report naming one sign does not always imply the global finding, so they are not merged.
These are disease labels inferred from a sign (hyperinflation), not terminology variants.
Clinical disease versus the radiographic sign.
Enlarged cardiomediastinum also covers the mediastinum, and the chamber enlargements are subtypes of cardiomegaly.

Widening of the superior mediastinum is close to 'superior mediastinal enlargement', but that class also covers a discrete mass. Enlarged cardiomediastinum includes the heart. Not merged, to stay strict.
Unfolding is elongation without dilatation, so it is a different finding, even though the two are sometimes confused.
Hilar enlargement is a sign. The others are distinct causes (nodes, arteries, venous congestion).
Parent and child subtypes with distinct appearances.
Lung opacity is an umbrella term. Pneumonia is a diagnosis, not the consolidation sign. GGO is a different density.
Explicitly separate etiologic classes.
Appearance versus diagnosis. Multiple nodules have many causes.

Eventration is one cause of elevation, often with a focal contour bulge. These are related, not synonyms.
Chilaiditi is the classic mimic of pneumoperitoneum, a different finding.

Sternal wires are often called 'sternal cerclage' in reports and look identical. However, the cerclage class also covers rib fixation and is defined by fracture fixation, so they are not merged. This is a borderline call.
Cerclage is a subtype of osteosynthesis.
